notes.title: Beam Eye Tracker v2.4.2: Faster Game Integration & Foveated Rendering Support
notes.content:
Beam Eye Tracker v2.4.2 is here, now with an upgraded API & SDK v2.0 for seamless game integration and foveated rendering support for game devs.

[h1]New API & SDK v2.0 Brings Powerful Upgrades for Game and Extension Developers[/h1]
- Foveated rendering support for more frames along with dynamic user interfaces for less visual clutter.
- Ability to start Beam and initiate eye tracking directly from within the game or extension.
- Improved camera controls with significantly lower latency. Easy recalibration and recentering functionality.
- Includes ready-to-use samples for quick integration into popular game engines.

[h1]User Experience Enhancements[/h1]
- Eye tracking overlay now scales with screen size for a more consistent experience.
- The demo no longer expires after 14 days. Playtime is only counted when the webcam is active.

[h1]Bug Fixes[/h1]
- Resolved crashes occurring on PCs due to folder names containing special characters.

[h1]Deprecation Notice[/h1]
- SDK v1.0 will be deprecated starting September 2025. Please update your integrations to SDK v2.0.

Your voice matters! Share this and tag your favorite game devs and ask for Beam Eye Tracker support: more immersion, more frames, effortless integration.

notes.title: Enhanced Webcam Compatibility
notes.content:
We are excited to announce this major update, which expands Beam's compatibility with an even wider range of webcams, making it easier than ever to use your preferred setup with the Beam Eye Tracker.

[h1]Enhanced Webcam Compatibility
[/h1]
[list]
[*] Beam now supports more webcam devices, including the OBS virtual camera, PS3 Eye Camera (when using the universal driver: [url=https://github.com/jkevin/PS3EyeDirectShow/releases]https://github.com/jkevin/PS3EyeDirectShow/releases[/url]) and other devices that rely on DirectShow drivers.
[*] The "Shared" camera access mode has been enhanced for better compatibility with other applications that access and control your webcam.
[*] [i]Steam Version only[/i]: The “Eyeware camera” virtual camera is now fully functional.
[/list]

[h1]UX Enhancements[/h1]
[list]
[*] If Beam is already running, attempting to launch it again will bring up the tray window or sign-in dialog, making it easier for users to find and access Beam.
[*] The default eye tracking overlay color has been updated to the brand accent color.
[*] [i]Standalone Version only[/i]: Clicking the tray icon now also brings up the sign-in page, providing a more intuitive user experience.
[/list]

[h1]Bug Fixes[/h1]
[list]
[*] [i]Standalone Version only[/i]: Some users experienced Beam crashing at startup (the tray icon would appear for a few seconds and then disappear closing Beam). This was fixed by disabling offline access on the specific PC on a case-by-case basis (the majority of users won’t have this issue). The video preview link has been updated.
[*] Improved logging capabilities for more efficient troubleshooting in the future.
[/list]

notes.title: 0% GPU Load
notes.content:
We are excited to announce the release of Beam Eye Tracker v2.2.0. This update ensures 0% GPU load for the Eye Tracking Overlay and all other functionalities, except for the Privacy Filter feature, while bringing other enhancements designed to improve your tracking experience with minimal system impact.


[h2]Eye Tracking Overlay Optimizations[/h2]

[list]
[*] 0% GPU Usage for Eye Tracking Overlay: We've reduced the GPU load to 0% by shifting processing to the CPU, now requiring only an additional 1-3% CPU usage depending on your processor.
[*] Increased Frame Rate and Responsiveness: The overlay now operates at the camera's FPS, providing smoother motion and significantly lower latency. Previously, it was capped at 30fps to reduce processing demands on the GPU.
[*] Resolved Compatibility Issues: We've resolved the notorious "Black Screen Issue" associated with outdated drivers by eliminating the dependence on OpenGL.
[*] Overlay Behavior Adjustments: Optimized to disappear seamlessly when hidden, especially during recording sessions with OBS, to enhance recording clarity.
[/list]

[h2]UX and Performance Enhancements[/h2]

[list]
[*] Improved Guidance for Users: A new first-time popup guide has been introduced for the eye tracking overlay to facilitate user onboarding.
[*] Enhanced Visual Quality: GIFs on feature cards are now rendered with higher quality, ensuring a more visually appealing experience.
[/list]

[h2]Bug Fixes[/h2]

[list]
[*] Gaming Extensions API Correction: Fixed a bug that prevented the Gaming Extensions API from updating correctly with the main screen, thereby enhancing accuracy and reliability in tracking.
[/list]

notes.title: Multilingual Support for Beam Eye Tracker v2.1.0
notes.content:
[h2]Multilingual support[/h2]

[list]
[*] Added support for 10 languages: English, Chinese, Russian, Spanish, Portuguese, German, French, Japanese, Korean, and Italian.
[*] Beam Eye Tracker by default will now use your Windows system language. You can change this in the Settings under General > System (scroll to the bottom). Make sure to restart the app for language settings to take effect.
[*] Note: Languages have been mostly auto-translated. Please report any major errors for correction.
[/list]

[h2]Bug Fixes[/h2]

[list]
[*] Calibration when using the Beam Eye Tracker iOS app extension without a connection has been improved to halt properly if disconnected.
[/list]

notes.title: Beam Eye Tracker 2.0: New Branding, Multi-Camera Support
notes.content:
[h1][b]No Webcam! No Problem.[/b][/h1]

We've enhanced user experience and simplified branding by merging our iOS and Webcam editions into a streamlined app. Now, it's easier to start with support for more input devices, including webcam apps and the iOS Beam Eye Tracker app extension, broadening accessibility and convenience for all users.


[h2]Simplified Branding, Unified Webcam & iOS Edition[/h2]
[list]
[*] The app has been rebranded to Beam Eye Tracker (by Eyeware) and now merges webcam and iOS editions into one comprehensive solution.
[*] The Beam Eye Tracker iOS app now serves as an extension to the Beam Eye Tracker enabling Face ID-equipped iPads/iPhones to function as eye trackers. This is a free upgrade. You can now offload processing and improve calibration robustness.
[*] The iOS app extension also acts as a virtual camera. You can use your iOS device as a regular webcam for other applications as well. Note: performance depends  on network speed.
[/list]
[h2]
UX Improvements[/h2]
[list]
[*] Updated user interface for a more sleek, modern look.
[*] When switching between webcams while in Exclusive access mode, the recommended format is now preselected. It prioritizes high frame rates and resolutions close to 720p.
[*] Settings window now enables mouse wheel scrolling across the entire interface, simplifying navigation without requiring cursor placement in specific scrollable areas.
[*] New "Tracked Eyes" option under Settings > General. Select 'Both' for optimal tracking robustness when possible. Choose 'Left Only' or 'Right Only' if you have one notably dominant eye.
[/list]
[h2]
Bug fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Solved an initialization issue which was preventing some users from starting the app.
[*] Ensured that the calibration window accepts the first click, which was being rejected randomly.
[*] Corrected virtual camera naming.
[/list]

[h2]Current limitations of iOS app extension[/h2]
[list]
[*] Productivity and Privacy features, as well as Tracked Eye selection are unavailable in the iOS app extension.
[*] Supports only 30fps at present
[*] Orientation is limited to landscape mode with the selfie notch on the right.
[/list]

notes.title: 60FPS+ Eye Tracking for Supported Webcams, 50% Reduced Jitter & Facecam Support
notes.content:
Eyeware Beam v1.6.0 is out and it's a doozy for this Black Friday.

[h2]Advanced Camera Management[/h2]
[list]
[*] 60FPS+ tracking on webcams that support higher frame rates. Make sure to set the performance mode to "high performance" for the best experience. 
[*] "Exclusive" and "Shared" mode are now available in the camera settings, with “Exclusive” allowing you to fix a custom resolution and framerate. Use "Eyeware camera" as your virtual cam in third-party apps when in “Exclusive” mode.
[*] In the "Preview" video it is now possible to change the format and exclusive access in real-time for quick testing.
[*] Elgato Facecam support and other UYVY video format webcams.
[/list]

[h2]Tracking Performance Improvements[/h2]
[list]
[*] 50% reduction in head tracking jittering.
[*] Smoothened eye tracking and reduced latency.
[*] Introducing sliders in Settings to adjust the filtering levels for head and eye tracking individually, allowing users to fine-tune the balance between smoothness and responsiveness.
[*] Latency reduction and minimization of lost frames sent to the API of gaming extensions.
[/list]

[h2]UX improvements[/h2]
[list]
[*] Removed startup pop-up to prevent disruptions when webcams or displays are unplugged. Alerts will now only appear during tracking activation.
[/list]

[h2]Bug Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Implemented fallback functionality for displays incompatible with the Windows API device enumeration.
[*] Resolved a startup issue linked to core selection on some systems.
[/list]

What features or updates would you like to see next? Let us know!
